newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines suspends peso-dlr trades for the day.
newsitem.headline: Philippines suspends peso-dlr trades for the day.

text.p: The Bankers Association of the Philippines said it has suspended peso-dollar trading for the rest of the day following the volatile movements of the peso.
Earlier, the bankers group had to temporarily halt trades after the peso moved beyond the limit allowed by the rules.
The peso tumbled when the Central Bank announced it was going to allow the peso to move in a new, wider range to quell peso speculation.
The peso had traded at 27/29.45, with volume reaching $27 million before trades stopped. The peso closed at 26.401 on Thursday.
Traders said the Central Bank unloaded about $1 billion in recent days to protect the peso, which some analysts said was also overvalued like Thailand.
On Thursday, the Central Bank had raised its overnight borrowing rate to its highest level of 32 percent since March 1995 in the wake of Mexico's financial crisis.
